author: reek
body: Tic-tac-toe rules on a 3x3 board. Board is a List Integer of 9 cells: 0=empty, 1=X, 2=O. Player 1 is X (maximizer), player 2 is O (minimizer). This chapter owns the rules: construction, legal moves, win detection. The built-in ttt-ai-move is a cheap positional heuristic that does not search and does not block threats; the game server uses it for fast stepping. Perfect play is ttt-perfect-ai in the Minimax chapter, which searches the complete game tree and is battery-verified to never lose.

author: reek
body: list-set-at mutates the list in place, so ttt-move copies the squares first. The copy is what makes ttt-move a value: search code applies candidate moves by the thousand to one live board and every caller keeps its own history.

author: reek
body: A positional heuristic: take the center, then a corner, then the first empty square. One board scan, no search, no threat detection - fast and beatable by design.
